package_info.package_versions: Unknown (affected Mac and Windows versions distributed prior to March 30th, 2023)
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CX Desktop App was compromised through a software supply chain attack, resulting in the distribution of malicious code embedded within trusted application binaries. Attackers inserted malware into the app during the build process, which was then delivered to end users via official update mechanisms. This enabled the execution of unauthorized code on user systems, facilitating targeted information theft and data exfiltration.

execution_context.trigger: post-launch (after application startup, during runtime operation)
execution_context.file_location: Electron app binary (malicious logic embedded in a bundled resource or third-party dependency, responsible for downloading and executing external payloads)
required_permissions: network (to download external files and exfiltrate data)
filesystem (to write and execute downloaded payloads)
environment_vars (to access sensitive user or system information)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The compromised 3CX Desktop App contains logic that, after launch, downloads a file from a public GitHub repository named 'IconStorages'. This file is disguised as an icon or image but actually contains an encrypted or obfuscated executable payload. The app then loads and executes this payload, which performs malicious actions such as information theft and data exfiltration.
malicious_snippets.code_language: JavaScript (Electron app logic invoking native code or shellcode via Node.js APIs; downloaded payload may be compiled binary or shellcode)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime after application launch, the code downloads a file from the 'IconStorages' GitHub repository, interprets it as an icon, decrypts and loads the embedded executable payload, and executes it, resulting in the theft of sensitive information and exfiltration to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The application downloads a file from an external, non-official public GitHub repository at runtime and executes its contents, which is highly atypical for legitimate Electron apps. The file is disguised as an icon but contains executable code, indicating an attempt to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Electron applications may download images or icons for UI purposes, but they should never execute code from such files, especially when sourced from untrusted, public repositories. Executing code from externally downloaded resources is a severe violation of secure software practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate applications may fetch icons or images from trusted sources for UI updates, but they do not execute code from these files. Any code execution from downloaded image files is highly abnormal and indicative of malicious intent.
key_indicators: Runtime download of files from public GitHub repositories (e.g., 'IconStorages')
Execution of code or payloads embedded within files masquerading as images or icons
Decryption or unpacking of downloaded files prior to execution
Network requests to GitHub immediately after application launch
Use of benign-sounding repository names to disguise malicious intent

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into the 3CX Desktop App or one of its dependencies during the build process, compromising the application before distribution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of compromised application binaries to end users via official channels

attack_chain.action: End users install or update the 3CX Desktop App, receiving the compromised binary through trusted update mechanisms.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious logic on user systems upon application launch

attack_chain.action: After application launch, the compromised app downloads a file from the 'IconStorages' GitHub repository, treating it as an icon but actually loading and executing the embedded malware payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the malware payload on the user's system

attack_chain.action: The executed malware payload performs information theft, targeting sensitive data (such as credentials or business information), and exfiltrates the stolen data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration and potential further compromise of affected organizations

behavioral_signatures: Electron-based application downloading files from public GitHub repositories (e.g., 'IconStorages') at runtime
Execution of code or payloads from files masquerading as images or icons
Decryption or unpacking of downloaded files prior to execution
Unexpected network requests to GitHub or other non-official sources immediately after application launch
file_indicators: Files downloaded from github.com/username/IconStorages or similarly named repositories
Icon or image files with embedded executable content (e.g., PE, Mach-O, or shellcode signatures within image files)
Presence of decrypted or unpacked payloads in temporary or application data directories
network_indicators: Outbound connections from the 3CX Desktop App process to attacker-controlled infrastructure for data exfiltration
Unusual HTTP(S) requests to domains not associated with 3CX or its official update infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Electron-based applications for runtime downloads of files from public repositories, especially when such files are used as icons or images but contain executable content. Flag any execution of code from externally downloaded resources, particularly those masquerading as images. Correlate network activity from the 3CX Desktop App process to known attacker infrastructure and monitor for unexpected access to public GitHub repositories. Analyze downloaded files for embedded executable content and track the creation or execution of new processes originating from the app.
